sections.title: The letter ene
paragraphs: The name of this letter is (ene) /ˈɛni/. Its main sound is a consonant, as in (noite) /ˈnoj.tɨ/, which means night. A consonant is a sound made when the mouth blocks or narrows the air. This letter has two different sounds.

sections.title: Making the sounds
paragraphs: For the first sound, press the tip of your tongue against the ridge behind your upper teeth. Let the air pass out through your nose. A nasal is a sound where the air goes out through the nose. Turn your voice on. Touch your throat to feel it shake. For the other sound, keep your tongue low and let the air escape through your nose and mouth together.

sections.title: Reading this letter
paragraphs: Before a vowel, you pronounce this letter as a consonant. You hear this sound /n/ in (ano) /ˈɐ.nu/. At the end of a syllable, the letter is not pronounced as a consonant. Instead, it turns the vowel before it into a nasal vowel. A nasal vowel is a vowel where air goes out through the nose and the mouth at the same time. You hear this in (canto) /ˈkɐ̃.tu/ and (ponte) /ˈpõ.tɨ/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: At the end of a syllable, do not tap your tongue to the roof of your mouth like in tent or plant. Keep your tongue down and let the air flow through your nose. Before a vowel, say it like the first sound in name.
